human_reorganization: All Hilbert products, adjoints and self-adjointness assertions are REAL on complex L2 classes, matching the formal scalar structure. The signed form is its real bilinear form, not an unasserted complex operator identification.

The actual distributional embedding has density u*K^2 against Lebesgue measure, with bounded drift 2*sign(K)*Kprime against absolute density. It is not the potentially undefined unweighted distribution represented by u.

The core derivative is first shown representative independent through the weak graph. Its original graph closure is included in the closed weak derivative; equality is not asserted. Dense Schwartz inputs are justified by finite Radon regularity and mollification.

The explicit coordinate probes w*conjugate(phi) and -w*conjugate(phi-prime)-b*conjugate(phi) are human Riesz-coordinate deductions proved by their pairings. They are total in H, not claimed to be a graph core for the adjoint.
The exact signed-adjoint domain is sign-transport of the Hilbert adjoint domain. The positive energy uses the Hilbert adjoint Dstar D rather than the signed divergence.

The complete Hilbert energy proof regroups actual closed-graph projection, weak variational identity, full product domain and resolvent-range argument. Positive quadratic form is not positivity preservation or an identified Markov generator.

The residual-squared test gives a shorter human proof of the actual polynomial Stein ODE. The normalized explicit signed example has a simple zero and L1 but non-L2 score. No simple-zero or non-L2-score assertion is made for every higher-heat kernel.
Hamza and fundamental-symmetry mechanisms are classical antecedents. Bounded-interval weighted relaxation and Krein coupling/spectral theorems are not transferred to the original global graph.

The explicit eta cutoff realizes the same smooth compact radius-one/two witness and unit derivative as the formal bump construction. The full-support Gaussian/Dirac mixture uses REAL L2 and is separately a well-defined but nonclosable derivative; the pure Dirac example instead fails representative independence. Neither is identified with an absolute Schwartz-density space.

The actual mixed-measure derivative is closable on every finite-dimensional domain subspace, whose directed family covers the original domain, while the union remains nonclosable by the same shrinking jets. Eventual escape of those jets from each fixed finite window is explicitly labelled a human classical subsequence consequence.

The positive generic criterion retains exact input-compatible bounded Q_i, energy-contracting linear P_i, local closability and pointwise fixed-window coverage. The printed two-limit proof needs no ordering, countability, uniform bound on Q_i or idempotence of P_i. Finite subspace coverage alone is not substituted for these assumptions.

Positive derivative-form closability is equivalent to sequential operator closability when the target is complete and the coefficient is positive; the zero coefficient carries no operator information. The real mixed-measure example remains distinct from the original complex-valued real Hilbert absolute-density space.

Primary Alberti–Bate–Marchese Corollary 1.6 supplies broader classical necessity context, with C_c^1 domain and its own defined topologies. No general singular-measure classification is derived or attributed to this companion.

Section 9 realizes the closed graph projection Phi(x)=(Rx,DRx) by a finite/countable independent-Gaussian series in an explicit orthonormal basis of the real Hilbert product. This is a human coordinate realization of the source isonormal embedding, with actual L2 values and finite-dimensional Gaussian laws.

The exact covariance <x,Ry>, strict variance, Green identity on the full domain of A=D*D and auxiliary first-chaos derivative/divergence/recovery are reconstructed with original graph limits. The auxiliary Gaussian derivative is not identified with the spatial weighted derivative.

A labelled human general D=0 infinite-dimensional counterexample uses independent Borel-Cantelli to separate a Hilbert-indexed Gaussian field from a Hilbert-valued Gaussian random variable. No assertion that the specific signed-density resolvent is the identity or is trace class is made. Neither auxiliary positivity nor covariance creates a positive original signed process law.

Section 7 reconstructs actual source dyadic scale 2^(-n), scaled-graph projection and native unscaled output. Strong value approximation holds on the whole Hilbert space; original graph approximation holds only on the original domain via the adjoint resolvent identity. The adjoint-density and pairing test are proved directly from the closed graph and its orthogonal complement. Bounded-output subsequences force native domain membership by dense extension and Riesz representation; outside-domain outputs escape to infinity. Uniformly bounded outputs converge weakly, not necessarily strongly. The diagonal ell2 example is a labelled elementary human illustration, not an added formal source result. Weighted-output vanishing never extends the original derivative.

Section 14 reconstructs the full three-state Gamma module with actual uniform probability, all-L2 bounded test algebra, weighted matrix positivity and scalar closability.
